title: A Living City Under the Waves: Why Coral Reefs Matter More Than They Look
title_zh: 海浪之下的活城市：珊瑚礁为何比看上去更重要
intro_zh: 本文约 533 词，重点词 6 个，句子难度适中（3/5），理解难度约 85%–90%，适合 CET-4 阅读训练。

paragraphs.en: Divers often describe a coral reef as a city under the sea, and the comparison is surprisingly accurate. Although reefs cover less than one percent of the ocean floor, they provide food and shelter for about a quarter of all marine species. Take the reef away, and the whole neighborhood falls apart.
paragraphs.zh: 潜水员常常把珊瑚礁形容为海底的城市，而这个比喻准得令人意外。珊瑚礁占据的海底面积不到百分之一，却为约四分之一的海洋物种提供食物和栖身之所。一旦礁体消失，整个“街区”都会随之瓦解。

paragraphs.en: First, it is worth clearing up a common misunderstanding. Coral is not a rock, and it is not a plant. It is a colony of tiny animals called polyps. Each polyp builds a hard cup of limestone around itself, and millions of these cups together form the reef. Inside the tissue of the polyps live microscopic algae that give coral both its color and most of its food.
paragraphs.zh: 首先，有一个常见的误解值得澄清：珊瑚既不是石头，也不是植物，而是由名叫“珊瑚虫”的小动物组成的群体。每只珊瑚虫都会在自己周围筑起一个坚硬的石灰质小杯，数以百万计的小杯共同构成了礁体。在珊瑚虫的组织里住着微小的藻类，它们赋予珊瑚颜色，也提供它大部分的食物。

paragraphs.en: This partnership explains why reefs matter so much. The algae make sugar from sunlight, while the polyps offer protection and nutrients in return. The result is a structure so rich in biodiversity that scientists still find new creatures there every year: small fish, shrimps, crabs, and animals that hide in the cracks.
paragraphs.zh: 这种共生关系解释了珊瑚礁为何如此重要。藻类利用阳光制造糖分，珊瑚虫则以保护与养分作为回报。结果便是一座生物多样性极高的结构体，科学家每年仍能在其中发现新的生物：小鱼、虾、蟹，以及藏在缝隙里的各种动物。

paragraphs.en: Reefs are also nurseries. Many fish that people eat, such as groupers and snappers, spend their first months among coral branches before swimming out to the open sea. Without that shelter, young fish become easy prey, and the fishing industry loses its future catch. A reef is, in other words, a habitat that pays for itself.
paragraphs.zh: 珊瑚礁也是“育幼场”。人们常吃的石斑鱼、笛鲷等鱼类，在游向开阔海域之前，会先在珊瑚枝间度过最初几个月。没有这层庇护，幼鱼很容易被吃掉，渔业也就失去了未来的渔获。换句话说，珊瑚礁是一种能自己“挣回本钱”的栖息地。

paragraphs.en: Second, reefs protect coastlines. A healthy reef can absorb up to ninety-seven percent of a wave's energy. That is why beaches behind reefs suffer far less erosion during storms. In countries such as Indonesia and the Philippines, hundreds of millions of people live close to the shore and depend on this natural barrier. In fact, engineers sometimes build artificial reefs to copy the protection that nature provides for free.
paragraphs.zh: 其次，珊瑚礁守护着海岸线。健康的礁体能吸收高达百分之九十七的海浪能量，这就是为什么礁体之后的海滩在风暴中遭受的侵蚀要小得多。在印度尼西亚、菲律宾等国家，数亿人住在离海岸不远的地方，依赖着这道天然屏障。事实上，工程师有时会建造人工礁，去复制大自然免费提供的这种保护。

paragraphs.en: Third, reefs bring in money. Diving, snorkeling, and reef-related fishing attract visitors from around the world and support millions of jobs, from boat captains to hotel cooks. According to one widely quoted estimate, reefs provide goods and services worth about 375 billion dollars a year. Chemicals taken from reef animals have also become medicines, including treatments for pain and some cancers. One researcher described the reef as a library we have barely begun to read.
paragraphs.zh: 第三，珊瑚礁带来经济收益。潜水、浮潜以及和珊瑚礁相关的渔业吸引着世界各地的游客，并支撑着数百万个工作岗位，从船长到酒店厨师。据一个被广泛引用的估算，珊瑚礁每年提供的商品与服务价值约3750亿美元。从礁区动物中提取的化学物质还变成了药物，包括止痛药和某些抗癌药。一位研究者把珊瑚礁形容为一座我们才刚刚开始翻阅的图书馆。

paragraphs.en: Yet reefs are in trouble. When the sea grows too warm, coral pushes out the algae living inside it and turns white. Scientists call this bleaching, and it can kill a reef. The Great Barrier Reef suffered back-to-back bleaching events in 2016 and 2017. Pollution, too much fishing, and anchors dropped on coral add to the pressure, and some reefs may not survive.
paragraphs.zh: 然而，珊瑚礁正陷入困境。当海水变得过热，珊瑚会把体内的藻类排出，自己也随之变白。科学家称之为“白化”，它能致礁体于死地。大堡礁在2016年和2017年连续遭遇白化事件。污染、过度捕捞，以及抛在珊瑚上的船锚，都在加重压力，有些珊瑚礁或许无法存活下来。

paragraphs.en: The good news is that reefs can recover if we give them a chance. Marine protected areas, cleaner rivers, and coral nurseries, where young corals are grown and then replanted, are already working in parts of the Caribbean and Australia. Daily choices help as well: using less plastic, saving water, and choosing sunscreen that is safe for reefs.
paragraphs.zh: 好消息是，只要给它机会，珊瑚礁是可以恢复的。海洋保护区、更洁净的河流，以及把幼珊瑚培育后再种回海里的珊瑚苗圃，已在加勒比海和澳大利亚的部分地区取得成效。日常选择同样有帮助：少用塑料、节约用水、选择对珊瑚礁无害的防晒霜。

paragraphs.en: A reef looks like stone, but it is really a living city built by animals no bigger than a grain of rice. Protecting it is not only about beautiful scenery. It is about food, safety, and the coastlines where millions of people live.
paragraphs.zh: 珊瑚礁看起来像石头，其实是一座由比米粒还小的动物建起的活城市。保护它，不只是为了留住美丽的风景，更是为了食物、安全，以及数百万人生存其间的海岸线。

questions.q: What is the main purpose of the passage?
options: To explain why coral reefs matter and how they can be protected.
To describe every kind of fish that lives on a coral reef.
To argue that diving and tourism should be limited near reefs.
To compare coral reefs with tropical rain forests.
questions.explain: 全文从珊瑚的本质、生态价值、护岸作用、经济与药用价值推进到白化危机和保护办法，主旨是说明珊瑚礁的重要性及如何保护，故选第一项。其余选项只是文中细节或文中未提。

questions.q: According to the passage, what is coral?
options: A kind of rock shaped by ocean waves.
A plant that grows in warm, shallow water.
A large fish that builds cups of limestone.
A colony of tiny animals called polyps.
questions.explain: 第二段明确指出珊瑚不是石头也不是植物，而是由名为 polyps（珊瑚虫）的小动物组成的群体，每只珊瑚虫筑起石灰质小杯。故选第四项。

questions.q: What can be inferred about the relationship between coral and the algae inside it?
options: The coral eats the algae and finally destroys them.
The algae give coral color and food, while coral gives them shelter.
They compete with each other for sunlight in the same area.
The algae can only live in very cold sea water.
questions.explain: 第二、三段说明藻类为珊瑚提供颜色和大部分食物，珊瑚虫则提供保护与养分，属于互利共生，因此可推断第二项正确。

questions.q: The word 'bleaching' in Paragraph 7 most probably refers to ______.
options: the sea becoming clearer and warmer
fish leaving a reef in large numbers
coral turning white after losing the algae inside it
scientists cleaning coral that has been damaged
questions.explain: 第七段指出海水过热时珊瑚排出体内藻类并变白，科学家称之为 bleaching（白化），故第三项最符合词义。
